messages:
Evelyn: heads-up — new user hit mypy/pyright error using the Python sampleapp after pip install. Looks like autogenerated stubs don't reflect Optional fields in models used by async streams.
Kai: can you paste a tiny repro?
Evelyn: minimal repro below:
```py
from typing import Optional, Dict
from pydantic import BaseModel

class Event(BaseModel):
    id: str
    meta: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None

async def consume(client):
    async for e in client.events_stream():
        # mypy: Item "None" of "Optional[Dict[str, str]]" has no attribute "items"
        for k, v in e.meta.items():
            pass
```
Evelyn: mypy output: 
main.py:9: error: Item "None" of "Optional[Dict[str, str]]" has no attribute "items"  [attr-defined]
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 1 source file)
Kai: sounds like a stub/runtime mismatch. Do the .pyi files mark meta as Optional? Also some streams emit heartbeat None wrappers in older runtime builds.
autogen-bot: FYI: current autogen pyi generator emits Event.meta as Dict[str, str] in some codepaths when default is None — bug tracked. Also some stream endpoints are typed AsyncIterator[Event] but at runtime can yield None for control frames.
Evelyn: that explains it. Short-term we can add a guard in sampleapp (`if e.meta:`) or `assert e.meta is not None` to quiet mypy. But new users running mypy --strict will fail during onboarding.
Kai: plan: PR to autogen generator to always emit Optional[...] for fields with default None, and audit streaming APIs to use AsyncIterator[Optional[Event]] when control frames are possible. Add a mypy/pyright check in autogen CI with a tiny sampleapp to catch regressions.
ci-bot: CI:autogen-tests failed mypy-suite (https://ci.example/runner/983) :warning:
docs-bot: added onboarding note + a sample mypy.ini to docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/431
Evelyn: filed SDK issue with repro + CI link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/833 — adding the failing sample and output. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
